hub_taildep.note: lambda_U is P(other node in its own top 1% | this node in its top 1%) on 15-min RTM prices; Pearson is on daily hours in the top 1% and is shown only as the contrast -- it answers a different question.

nodal_hub_test.note: DAM hourly. 'own hub' = argmax lambda_U over hubs (see module docstring): an upper bound on hub-hedge coverage, not ERCOT's hub mapping. With 1 month(s) loaded the q=0.99 conditioning sample is only ~7 hours, so q=0.95 is reported alongside.

basis_four_leg.note: the 'uncorrelated' leg uses lambda_U between BASIS series (does my local congestion arrive when everyone else's does); lambda_u_median_price is the same statistic on raw prices, shown for contrast.

tail_index.note: Hill alpha on the top 1% of 15-min RTM prices per node-year. The offer cap truncates the tail, so alpha is not comparable across cap eras (see config.HCAP_SCHEDULE); node-years whose top 1% is pinned against the cap are flagged censored and left out of the yearly medians.

fourcp.note: ERCOT load is hourly and forward-filled onto the 15-min grid, so a CP is resolved to its peak HOUR (4 intervals). D3's top-30 window is ex post and catches 4/4 by construction; these rules are ex ante.
